fields.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
fields.note: The guide supports the core requirement and the listed causes (A–R). It also supports the Notice to Quit rule, the self-help ban, relocation of six times monthly rent with 18% interest, treble damages, the $10,000 penalty, rooming house notice, and landlord registration. The 'illegal occupancy' relocation point and the 'treble damages for misuse after owner-occupancy eviction' point are both in the document.

fields.quoted_span:
A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit 
for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
fields.note: Most periods match: 3 days, 1 month, 2 months, 3 months, 18 months, 3 years, 6x rent relocation and the $10,000 penalty. One mismatch: the 3-day group is lumped with 'criminal causes' and the 2-month group is described loosely. The 1-month group correctly includes habitual late payment. The 3-day group omits drug, assault, theft offenses by name but 'criminal causes' covers them. The 'penalty up to $10,000' applies only to the retirement/demolition re-use violation, which the summary does not make clear.
The rule's effective_date is null, and the guide states no effective date for the Anti-Eviction Act.

fields.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act,  N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect 
blameless tenants from eviction
fields.note: The guide presents the Act as current law with no sign of repeal or sunset, which is consistent with 'in_force'.

fields.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family 
homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes. This 
law also applies to rooming and boarding homes
fields.note: Single-family, mobile homes, apartments, rooming/boarding, the hotel/motel continual-residence rule, and the trust exemption are all supported. The owner-occupied exclusion is stated hedgily ('may not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units'), and the guide separately says those tenants are covered by 2A:18-61.2(a), which the rule reflects. The rule states 'excluded' more firmly than the guide's 'may not apply'.

fields.note: The primary citation 2A:18-61.1 and the aliases (2A:18-53, 2A:18-61.2, 2A:18-61.6, N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c), 5:26-3.4(c)) all appear in the guide. 'P.L.1974, c.49' does not appear in the document, but it is only an alias.
